name: Vaelora: The Living Realm
description: A true medieval sandbox from muddy field to royal throne. Begin as a tenant, outlaw, knight, merchant, healer, soldier, noble, prince or sovereign in a persistent realm of law, war, trade, seasons, succession and consequences.

schedule.activity: Setting type at the print shop

startingLives.name: Tenant of Dunmere
startingLives.description: Begin at first light in a wet field, owing rent and labor but knowing every person and path in the vale.
startingLives.intro: Dawn finds you ankle-deep in the east barley strip, where last night’s rain has laid half the young crop flat. The reeve’s tally stick waits on the boundary stone. So does a black feather—the sign Blackbriar uses when it wants a private word. Behind you, Dunmere’s rent bell begins to ring.

startingLives.name: Blackbriar Outlaw
startingLives.description: Begin wanted in a forest camp where stolen food, desperate families and ambitious killers share one fire.
startingLives.intro: Someone has dragged a bound royal courier into Blackbriar before breakfast. Half the camp wants his pay chest. Rook Harrow wants to know why the courier was riding alone—and why the sealed letter in his boot names you.

startingLives.name: Landless Knight
startingLives.description: Begin with a horse, armor, an honorable name and no money to maintain any of them.
startingLives.intro: Your horse throws a shoe beside the Old King’s Road milestone at the exact moment three riders appear behind you wearing no colors. Ahead, a royal recruiting sergeant is nailing a call to arms over a reward notice bearing a very good likeness of one of those riders.

startingLives.name: Royal Household Guard
startingLives.description: Begin inside Crownfast, close enough to power to see fear beneath ceremony.
startingLives.intro: The queen’s door is open. It is never open. Ser Calder stands in the corridor with blood on one cuff and orders you to close the stair, admit no councillor, and tell no one what you heard from inside.

startingLives.name: Guild Merchant
startingLives.description: Begin with credit, contracts and a cargo whose price could decide whether a district eats.
startingLives.intro: Your warehouse key turns, but the door opens from inside. Forty sacks of contracted grain are gone. In their place sits a royal treasury chest, sealed and very much not yours, while the guild bell summons every master to an emergency vote.

startingLives.name: Priory Healer
startingLives.description: Begin in sanctuary with medical knowledge, vows of aid and fugitives whose stories do not agree.
startingLives.intro: Three patients arrive before dawn: a feverish child, a customs officer with an arrow in his back, and the masked archer who shot him. Priory law protects them both until sunrise. Outside, mounted officers demand the door.

startingLives.name: Fen Boat Runner
startingLives.description: Begin on hidden waterways with contraband, cousins at every toll and debts that cannot be settled in coin.
startingLives.intro: The tide uncovers a body beneath your boat landing, dressed in guild blue and holding your genuine customs permit. Across the channel a crown patrol is already turning toward Mirecross.

startingLives.name: March Levy
startingLives.description: Begin cold, underpaid and armed at the edge of a war whose causes are being argued far away.
startingLives.intro: The dawn muster calls one hundred and ninety-eight names. Two hundred answered yesterday. Your file leader quietly shows you blood beneath the supply wagon and asks whether you want the officers to find it first.

startingLives.name: Heir of Stagwatch
startingLives.description: Begin responsible for a struggling estate, its tenants, its debts and a dangerous blood claim.
startingLives.intro: Breakfast is interrupted by three arrivals: a guild banker with the estate debt, the reeve with news that tenants hid seed grain, and a royal herald carrying a summons addressed not to Lady Mara—but to you.

startingLives.name: Royal Prince
startingLives.description: Begin close to succession, surrounded by affection, surveillance and people who need your future.
startingLives.intro: A servant wakes you before the bells with news that the queen is ill. On your writing desk lies a succession oath in the Chancellor’s hand, unsigned, and beneath it a second note offering enough soldiers to make the signature unnecessary.

startingLives.name: Sovereign of the Realm
startingLives.description: Begin on the throne with law, armies and wealth that are all less absolute than they look.
startingLives.intro: The council rises when you enter, but no one meets your eyes. On the table: an empty treasury report, a border demand for troops, a guild ultimatum over grain, and a sealed physician’s note marked for your hand alone. Outside, petitioners chant for bread.

startingLives.name: Unknown Wanderer
startingLives.description: Begin with almost nothing and no fixed identity. The world will decide who you are by what you do.
startingLives.intro: Rain follows you to a four-way milestone where a corpse hangs in a gibbet and someone has left a fresh loaf beneath it. The north road leads to the capital, east to war, south to the fen and west to a village ringing its rent bell. Hoofbeats approach from behind.

name: Bellwether, 2005 — A Suburban Life
description: A massive ensemble life simulator set in a complete American town in 2005: 243 explorable places, 296 scheduled residents, homes, schools, mall culture, work, family, local politics and no mandatory plot.

startingLives.name: The New Kid
startingLives.description: Your family moved to Bellwether yesterday. Nobody knows your history, and you do not yet know the map of theirs.
startingLives.intro: The guidance counselor mispronounces your last name over the intercom before first period. By lunch, three different people have invited you to three mutually incompatible tables—and somebody has written your old hometown beneath your locker number.

startingLives.name: Bellwether Lifer
startingLives.description: You know every shortcut and everybody knows a version of you, including several versions you would like retired.
startingLives.intro: Your car starts on the fourth try in the student lot. The morning announcement says the senior prank caused “significant plumbing consequences.” Your phone shows six missed calls, and the assistant principal is walking directly toward you.

startingLives.name: Middle-School Wildcard
startingLives.description: Your world is school, home, bikes, friends, older siblings and freedoms measured in blocks and minutes.
startingLives.intro: The bus pulls away with your science project still on it. Your best friend swears they can catch it by cutting through Briar Creek Woods. First bell is in twenty-two minutes, and the vice principal is already standing at the entrance.

startingLives.name: Suburban Parent
startingLives.description: A household, a job, a car, school logistics and thirty-seven small promises all compete for the same Tuesday.
startingLives.intro: At 7:14 Monday morning, the minivan will not start, one child says today is definitely picture day, your boss has left two voicemails, and the answering machine contains a message from Town Hall about “your fence situation.”

startingLives.name: Starting Over at Westgate
startingLives.description: You have an apartment, a child, two jobs between you and disaster, and no time for the town’s assumptions.
startingLives.intro: The radiator has stopped again. Your child’s school calls at the same moment the diner asks whether you can cover a shift, while a bright orange notice appears under the apartment door announcing a rent increase next month.

startingLives.name: First-Year Teacher
startingLives.description: You have one classroom, one contract year and roughly one hundred people evaluating your choices.
startingLives.intro: A parent is waiting outside your classroom before the first bell. Inside, someone has replaced every desk with a folding chair from the auditorium, and the principal’s memo says today’s unannounced observation will occur “at any time.”

startingLives.name: Mall Employee
startingLives.description: Your shifts, friends, romantic complications and entire social map overlap beneath one fluorescent roof.
startingLives.intro: The opening shipment contains two hundred copies of the wrong album. Your manager is stuck in traffic, a local band has arrived expecting the in-store performance nobody booked, and mall security wants to discuss footage from last night.

startingLives.name: Small Business Owner
startingLives.description: You have keys, payroll, regulars, debt and the freedom to work every hour the business is open.
startingLives.intro: The espresso machine makes a noise like a lawn mower and dies during the morning rush. At the same moment, a developer offers to buy your lease, and the health inspector joins the line.

startingLives.name: Local Reporter
startingLives.description: You can ask nearly anyone a question, but publishing the answer may cost access, advertising or friendships.
startingLives.intro: An envelope on your desk contains copies of a development contract dated three weeks before the public bidding process. The editor needs a zoning story by noon. The bank president is already calling to ask what you are working on.

startingLives.name: Night-Shift Officer
startingLives.description: You have authority, a radio, a partner and a town where every call may involve somebody you know.
startingLives.intro: Dispatch sends you to the mall for a “fountain-related disturbance” and then quietly adds that the mayor’s son is involved. Your partner recognizes the address on a second pending call and asks you to take the long route.

startingLives.name: Mayor of Bellwether
startingLives.description: You can set agendas and influence departments, but every promise has a budget, a constituency and a camera.
startingLives.intro: The council chamber microphones are live ten minutes early. Through them, half the town hears two council members arguing that your development deal is already fixed. Your assistant whispers that the state auditor has arrived without an appointment.

startingLives.name: Retired Local Fixture
startingLives.description: You have time, history, skills and connections spanning people who no longer speak to each other.
startingLives.intro: The diner waitress brings your usual before you order and slides a sealed letter beneath the coffee. It is addressed in the handwriting of a friend who died eight years ago. Across the counter, the new reporter is asking about the old factory fire.

startingLives.name: Emergency Doctor
startingLives.description: You carry expertise and responsibility inside a hospital woven tightly into the town outside it.
startingLives.intro: Three ambulances arrive within six minutes: a factory injury, a school-bus crash with no serious wounds, and the bank president complaining of chest pain while insisting his name stay off the board. Pediatrics has no overnight coverage.

startingLives.name: Back Home Again
startingLives.description: You returned to your childhood room with boxes, a résumé and a town determined to remember you at seventeen.
startingLives.intro: Your mother has circled three jobs in the Beacon and scheduled you for lunch with someone who “knows people.” Before you can object, your old best friend leaves a message asking whether you still have the key to the water tower fence.

startingLives.name: Lakeview Golden Child
startingLives.description: You have money, access and expectations high enough to make every mistake public.
startingLives.intro: A photo from Saturday’s lake party is circulating at school on printed computer paper. You are not doing anything illegal in it—but somebody important is visible behind you, and your parent wants every copy gone before lunch.

name: The Shattered Crown of Aldenmere
description: A complete three-act heroic-fantasy campaign: a murdered reeve, a silent mine, and a two-hundred-year-old debt coming due. Mystery, intrigue, and dungeon-delving — with endings won by sword or by insight.
intro:
The caravan pays you off at the crossroads milestone — eleven days guarding wool wagons for nine silver and a blister — and rolls on south toward Karsholm without you. You walk north into Emberwick under a dawn the color of forge-light.

The village should be waking. Instead it stands still in the square: forty-odd souls in mourning grey around a coffin on trestles, while a young priestess in dawn-gold vestments speaks the rites. The chapel bell tolls for the dead. You count the strokes the way every child of the Vale learns to — twelve, one for each god-hour.

It strikes a thirteenth time. Every head in the square lifts at once.

In the hush that follows, details find you. The mine on the hill above town — the Ironvein, whose ore pays for every roof here — has no smoke, no cart-rattle, no sound at all. At the square's edge a plump man in merchant's velvet is not mourning in the least; he is making small notes in a grain ledger, thumbing it from the wrong edge. And on the chapel steps a stable-child is staring not at the coffin but at you, with the fierce relief of someone who has been waiting for anyone at all to arrive.

The coffin holds Reeve Harlan Mosse, dead three nights past of what the village is calling a fall. The mine has been silent for nine days. The Gilded Griffin's door stands open behind you, and the smell of bread and beeswax drifts across the square like the last normal thing in the world.

What do you do?

name: Policy Panic at Bramble & Pike
description: A living small-town workplace comedy inside a dysfunctional regional insurance office. Join at any rung, survive absurd claims, romance coworkers, expose secrets, chase promotion, ruin the copier and reshape the whole branch.
intro:
Monday, 8:57 a.m. Rain needles the glass doors of Bramble & Pike Mutual while the lobby switchboard blinks like a tiny distress signal.

Gloria Bell sits behind the curved reception desk in magenta, perfectly composed, one manicured finger holding down three phone lines at once. She looks up at you with a smile that says she already knows why you are here—and probably knows a better reason you should leave.

Behind her, something heavy crashes in the bullpen. Eli Finch yelps. The copier begins emitting a continuous alarm. Denton Pike's voice rolls out of his office: “Nobody panic. This is what controlled momentum sounds like.”

Then a soaked woman from the state insurance commission walks through the door, shows Gloria a badge, and asks to see the branch manager.

It is not yet nine o'clock.

startingLives.name: The New Hire
startingLives.description: Start on your first morning with a desk, a training binder and no idea which warnings are jokes.

startingLives.name: Gloria’s Temporary Cover
startingLives.description: Gloria is away for one morning. You inherit the switchboard, the lobby and everyone’s assumption that the desk is easy.

startingLives.name: Field Claims Adjuster
startingLives.description: You know damaged homes, frightened clients and the difference between fraud and desperation. Mara wants your eyes on three roof claims.

startingLives.name: Hungry Sales Agent
startingLives.description: Connor’s numbers dominate the board and Denton just announced one promotion. You have a phone, a book of leads and reasons to need the money.

startingLives.name: State Examiner
startingLives.description: Arrive unannounced with authority to inspect the branch, interview staff and turn comedy into sworn testimony.

startingLives.name: After-Hours Cleaner
startingLives.description: You work when the masks come off, know what people throw away and possess keys nobody remembers issuing.

startingLives.name: The Owner’s Adult Child
startingLives.description: Your surname opens doors and closes conversations. Corporate sent you to Maplebridge to “learn the business,” and nobody agrees what that means.
